CORPUS_PARA: We built the pretraining corpus from the ComplexEye neutrophil migration release (Zenodo 10082674, CC BY 4.0): 288 of 302 movies processed without failure into **288,081 cell-centred clips** of 16x96x96 uint8 (42.48 GB) in 42 sequential shards. Cells were detected with a classical temporal-median/MAD pipeline and linked with trackpy; each clip follows its own track so the cell stays centred and the model cannot use frame drift as a shortcut. Clips were sampled at two strides, giving effective frame intervals of 8s (n=227,246), 24s (n=60,835). All frames are at 0.641 um/px against a 0.65 um/px target, so no resampling was applied. The corpus is single-source, which is a real limitation: it is one cell type (human neutrophils) under one imaging modality.
PRETRAIN_PARA: TiJepa-0 is a ViT-S (96x96 px, 16 frames, 2x8x8 tubelets, 1,152 tokens) trained with a V-JEPA-style objective: a context encoder sees visible tubelets, an EMA target encoder sees the whole clip, and a narrow predictor regresses the target encoder's latents at masked positions under an L1 loss. Masking is multi-block and tubed over time, so a masked cell cannot be copied from an adjacent frame. Training ran for **55,000 steps (24.44 effective epochs over the corpus) in 4.43 GPU-hours** on one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB in bf16, stopping on `max_steps`. Mean loss fell from 0.400 over the first 500 steps to 0.312 over the last 500. Embedding standard deviation and effective rank were logged throughout as collapse diagnostics (Figure 2); no collapse intervention was required. Pretraining used **seed 0 only**: the run had a single GPU, so the three-seed requirement was applied to all probes and downstream models instead, and single-seed pretraining is a limitation of this run.
BBBC_PARA:
We sampled 7,041 annotated cells across 60 fields of view, stratified by FOV and class, and cropped 96x96 px around each annotation. Replicate 1 contains only amoeboid vs round (no stratified cells are annotated in it), so the planned three-class probe is a two-class probe. All probes are FOV-grouped (never splitting a field of view across train and test), with cluster-bootstrap CIs over FOVs and a FOV-level permutation null.

| E1_handcrafted_morphology | 0.697 ± 0.000 | [0.678, 0.715] | 0.005 | -0.076 [-0.094, -0.058], p<0.0001 | -0.000 | 0.095 |
| E2_imagenet_vit_s | 0.755 ± 0.000 | [0.738, 0.772] | 0.005 | -0.017 [-0.036, 0.002], p=0.0690 | 0.197 | 0.234 |
| E3_dinov2_vit_s | 0.769 ± 0.000 | [0.755, 0.786] | 0.005 | -0.003 [-0.019, 0.014], p=0.7290 | 0.277 | 0.230 |
| E4_tijepa0 | 0.828 ± 0.000 | [0.814, 0.843] | 0.005 | +0.056 [0.045, 0.067], p<0.0001 | 0.083 | 0.110 |
| E5_tijepa0_frame_shuffled | N/A (undefined on static frames) | | | | | |
| E6_tijepa0_random_init | 0.772 ± 0.000 | [0.756, 0.790] | 0.005 | - (reference) | 0.100 | 0.065 |

The FOV-identity column matters: in BBBC054 each FOV *is* one exposure time, so an encoder that merely memorises fields of view would score well on exposure-time regression for the wrong reason. Chance for that probe is 0.017. The comparison that isolates pretraining from architecture is E4 against E6, the same network with random weights: +0.056 (95% CI [0.045, 0.067], p < 0.0001). Notably E6 alone is already competitive with DINOv2, so much of the performance on this task comes from the architecture and the probe rather than from either pretraining corpus. Crops were not resampled to a common micron scale because BBBC054 states a 20x objective but no pixel size; this is a recorded deviation.

The frame-shuffled control (E5) is meaningful here because the input is a genuine time series. CoTracker was not run (NOT RUN: dl.fbaipublicfiles.com unreachable in preflight).
B31_PARA:
The Tay-lab deposit (Zenodo 14337874, CC BY 4.0) provides single-cell NF-κB traces across sequential ligand pairs. The deposit ships no column dictionary, and the folder holding the human-readable condition labels was not deposited, so the matrix layout was reconstructed from the deposit's own MATLAB preprocessing script and the ligand code for LPS was identified by intersecting the second-ligand code sets of two deposit files with their file-name ligand sets. Analyses are restricted to the five files whose layout could be confirmed; the cytokine-block and sepsis files are flagged layout-unverified and excluded.

Classifying prior LPS exposure from the response to a second LPS stimulus at a matched 8 h interval (139 naive→LPS vs 172 LPS→LPS cells) gives a balanced accuracy of **0.701** ([0.643, 0.752]) from the raw trace and 0.598 ([0.566, 0.633]) from hand-crafted features. **Neither is significant**: the contrast rests on 4 wells, so a well-level permutation null is coarse and both give p = 0.30. We report the point estimates because the plan requires null results to be reported, not because they support a claim. First-ligand identity across 10 classes reaches 0.338 (chance 0.100); this is **not** comparable to the published 72.8% four-class figure, which uses a different class set and validation scheme.
B33_PARA: Regressing condition-level expression on condition-mean trace features with leave-one-condition-out ridge over 4 shared conditions gives a mean per-gene r of 0.055 and 86 genes with r > 0.5, **below** a condition-permutation null averaging 333.9 such genes (p = 0.49). This is a null result. The deposited RNA-seq contains no LPS→LPS sample, so the homologous tolerance contrast classified above has no matching transcriptome at all; the shared conditions are heterologous.
B4_PARA: Linking the mouse and human literatures was also null. In human (GSE58310, LPS-tolerised vs macrophage control, 4 donor-paired samples, 24,655 expressed genes) the pre-specified criteria of BH-FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1 return 0 up and 1 down genes; in mouse (heterologous primed->LPS (n=4) vs media->LPS (n=2); the deposit has no LPS->LPS sample) they return 1 up. The ortholog overlap is 0 genes. A clearly-labelled exploratory analysis using nominal p < 0.01 instead of FDR (34 human up genes) also gives an overlap of 0. The two contrasts are not the same biological comparison — the mouse one is heterologous priming, the human one homologous tolerance — and neither has the power to support an overlap test.
C1_PARA: Anchor signatures were derived from GSE46903 (Xue et al., human GM-CSF macrophages on GPL6947). All three anchors were taken at 72 h, the only time point at which ultrapure LPS samples exist in that series, against the matched unstimulated control: **S_LPS** from 6 upLPS vs 7 control samples; **S_IFNg** from 7 IFNg vs 7 control samples; **S_IL4** from 10 IL4 vs 7 control samples. Each signature is the top 100 up-regulated genes by Welch t among genes passing BH-FDR < 0.05. S_IFNg recovers canonical interferon-γ response genes (GBP5, GBP1, GBP4, GCH1, TAP1), which is a useful sanity check; S_LPS at 72 h does not recover acute LPS genes, consistent with the acute response having resolved by that time point, and this weakens the LPS half of the M1-like axis.
C2_PARA:
We scored every GSE58310 sample (Saeed et al.: naive monocytes, 6 d macrophage control, LPS-tolerised and β-glucan-trained, 4 donors each) with a rank-based singscore-style statistic, expressed relative to that dataset's own macrophage baseline. Rank-based scoring is what makes an array-derived signature comparable to RNA-seq at all.

| state | n | M1-like (95% CI) | M2-like (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| LPS tolerised | 4 | 0.0014 [-0.0029, 0.0058] | -0.0010 [-0.0083, 0.0065] |
| beta glucan trained | 4 | -0.0092 [-0.0135, -0.0041] | -0.0042 [-0.0119, 0.0036] |
| control | 4 | 0.0000 [-0.0028, 0.0033] | 0.0000 [-0.0098, 0.0095] |
| naive monocyte | 4 | 0.0191 [0.0119, 0.0259] | -0.0269 [-0.0414, -0.0152] |

The separations are small — hundredths of a unit on a rank scale whose range is ±0.5 — and the trained and tolerant states sit close to the macrophage baseline on both axes, with naive monocytes displaced furthest. Replication was not possible: NOT USABLE: the GEO series matrix contains no expression table (table_begin immediately followed by table_end) and no processed supplementary matrix is deposited NOT USABLE for gene-level scoring: only bigWig/bedGraph coverage tracks are deposited, no gene-level matrix
C3_PARA: **The projection into image space (C3) was not performed.** The planned two-axis projection requires image-space centroids for M0, M1 and M2 cells. The only public dataset providing images with those labels is Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.m0cfxpp8v, which was unreachable in this run (an Anubis proof-of-work challenge on every official download endpoint; see reports/MANUAL_DOWNLOADS.md). No accessible dataset substitutes for it: BBBC054 carries microglial morphology classes and LPS exposure time, not macrophage polarization states. Substituting it and presenting the result as the planned analysis would misrepresent what was measured, so the two-axis projection is left undone. Mapping omics coordinates into the learned image space requires image-side centroids for M0, M1 and M2 cells, and no accessible dataset in this run provides images labelled with those states. Rather than substitute a different label set and present it as the same analysis, the projection is left undone and the omics coordinates are reported on their own.
METHODS:
### 4.1 Compute and tier

1x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
(40960 MiB),
30 logical cores, 226.8 GB RAM.
Tier **T1** (exactly 1 GPU detected (40960 MiB); brief: 1 GPU -> T1), encoder ViT-S,
precision bf16, raw-video cap 120.0 GB.
PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8.
Seed policy: single GPU: pretraining uses seed 0 only; seeds 0/1/2 used for all probes and downstream models (must be stated in Methods).

### 4.2 Pretraining data and preprocessing

See §2.1. Detection used a temporal-median background with a MAD threshold and an area
filter; linking used trackpy (search radius 12 px, memory 2, minimum track length 16).
Cellpose was not used: the labelled evaluation sets need no segmentation (BBBC054 ships
annotated coordinates, S-BIAD2196 ships tracked instance masks), so a classical detector
kept the GPU free for training. The frame-QC classifier specified in the plan was **not**
trained, because only 5 of 8,441 S-BIAD2133 files could be retrieved in time; no QC
filtering was applied to pretraining clips.

### 4.3 Model and training

ViT-S encoder (384 dim, 12 layers, 6 heads) over 2x8x8 tubelets of 16x96x96 clips
(1,152 tokens), fixed 3D sine-cosine positional embeddings, EMA target encoder
(momentum 0.996 → 1.0), predictor of width 192 and depth 6,
multi-block tube masking, L1 loss on layer-normalised target latents, AdamW with cosine
schedule and warmup, bf16 autocast, gradient clipping at 1.0.

### 4.4 Probes and statistics

All encoders are frozen and every encoder gets the identical probe. Splits are grouped
at the highest available unit (FOV for BBBC054, well for Part B traces, movie for
tracking), never at the cell or frame level. Confidence intervals are cluster bootstraps
(2,000 resamples) at the grouping unit; "better than chance" is tested by permuting
labels at the group level; encoder comparisons use a paired cluster bootstrap on
identical resamples. Learned probes are run at seeds 0/1/2 and reported as mean ± sd.
For Part B, the logistic C was tuned once by inner CV and then held fixed inside the
permutation refits, which is a recorded deviation from per-fit tuning.

### 4.5 Licences of data and weights

Pretraining used only CC BY 4.0 data. Every dataset's licence was read from its own
record and is recorded in `manifests/datasets.yaml`; third-party model weights and their
licences are in `manifests/models.yaml`. The datasets the plan excluded
(Zenodo 16319732 CC BY-NC-ND, DeepCell DynamicNuclearNet, the Cellpose training set,
CTMC-v1, LIVECell, Cell Tracking Challenge) were not downloaded or used.
